tech-news.headline: OpenAI removes live internet access from frontier model training and moves agents to a cached offline web.

items.title: OpenAI cuts live internet from frontier training, builds offline web
items.body: OpenAI said it removed live internet access for all frontier models during training. Models now browse and search a large indexed, cached copy of the web. The change follows a September 20 DNS-resolver incident; frontier RL resumed on October 1. OpenAI now uses high-compute red-teaming as part of the safety case for frontier runs.
items.why: Teams that run agent training or evals can copy this pattern: cached web, no egress, red-team the sandbox.

items.title: OpenAI red-team agents find unauthenticated RCE in Brotli
items.body: OpenAI said its red-teaming exercise found a flaw in the Brotli compression library that allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Brotli is included in Node.js, Bun and Envoy. The same campaign found microVM escape chains and flaws in Kata Containers, gVisor, Docker and the Linux kernel, which led to patches and coordinated disclosures.
items.why: Brotli ships inside Node.js, Bun and Envoy, so patch pipelines and container images need a check.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.310 brings Monitor tool to Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry
items.body: Claude Code v2.1.310 makes the Monitor tool and plugin monitors work on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry. It fixes failures behind gateways that reject the effort beta value or mid-conversation system messages. Enterprise custom roles can now control access to cloud sessions and Remote Control.
items.why: Teams that run Claude Code through Amazon Bedrock now get background monitors and plugin monitors.

items.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation
items.body: Anthropic gave the Agent Skills standard, name, GitHub organization and agentskills.io domain to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation. More than 70 agent platforms use the format, 1 million skills are published and about 280 million installs are recorded. The roadmap adds versioned releases, a proposal process and security guidance for skill authors.
items.why: Skills become a vendor-neutral format, so one SKILL.md can serve Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot and Cursor.

items.title: Claude on Google Cloud, Anthropic-managed, adds Opus 5.5 Fast mode
items.body: Anthropic now operates the Claude API for customers who reach it through their Google Cloud project. Google Cloud IAM controls access and billing runs through Google Cloud Marketplace. Opus 5.5 Fast mode is available on this offering.
items.why: Multi-cloud teams can buy Claude through Google Cloud billing and IAM while Anthropic runs the API.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.309 hardens sandbox and MCP permissions
items.body: Shell startup files no longer run outside the sandbox before each command, and denyWrite patterns now apply through symlinks. Sandboxed commands and auto-accepted edits can no longer modify the --mcp-config file. On Windows, PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks no longer fail open when Git for Windows is missing.
items.why: Sandboxed agents can no longer change their own MCP config, which closes a privilege path in CI.

items.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed
items.body: Kimi K3.1 Pro is a 2.8T-parameter MoE model with 104B active parameters and a 1M-token context, priced at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens. Highspeed runs 2 to 3 times faster at $4 and $20. Moonshot reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 66.4% for Claude Opus 5.5. It is live on the Kimi API; open weights are expected in November 2026.
items.why: A 1M-context MoE model at $2/$10 per million tokens gives a cheaper option for agent coding workloads.

chips.headline: NVIDIA launches Minerva, an AIOps platform that traces slow AI jobs to the failing GPU, NIC or cable.

items.title: NVIDIA Minerva brings end-to-end observability to AI factories
items.body: Minerva joins telemetry from NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and jobs into a live knowledge graph of GPUs, SuperNICs, switches, cables and jobs. It processes billions of data points per hour with ML to detect anomalies, predict failures and group alerts into incidents with a likely root cause. IREN uses it now; IBM, Jio, Lambda and Tesla plan to deploy it, and Dell, Lenovo and Supermicro will offer it.
items.why: GPU cluster operators get one AIOps layer for root cause, failure prediction and automated fixes.

items.title: IQuest-Q1: open 320B MoE model built for agentic CLI work
items.body: IQuest-Q1 is a sparse MoE model with 320B total and 15B active parameters per token. Training used Stable SplitNorm, Muon and muP in pre-training, then context extension, then SFT plus domain RL across several agent scaffolds, with model merging of experts and checkpoints. The authors say it is open source; the abstract gives no benchmark scores.
items.why: An open agentic-coding MoE with 15B active parameters is cheap enough to self-host for terminal agents.

items.title: Deep Fusion Memory adds parametric knowledge without online retrieval
items.body: Deep Fusion Memory predicts a chunk-level memory from preceding context and fuses it into hidden states through gated cross-attention, with the backbone frozen. It needs 32 times fewer retrieval queries to build training data than token-level methods. It beats the strongest baseline on QA by 12.71% with Mistral-7B-v0.3 and 11.19% with Qwen3-8B-Base.
items.why: It can cut RAG retrieval cost in production by moving knowledge into a trained memory module.
items.source: Hugging Face Papers · Wei et al.

items.title: Tencent WeVisOne-VL unifies object and pixel perception
items.body: WeVisOne-VL is a vision-language model that unifies object-level and pixel-level perception, including detection, OCR, segmentation and matting. The authors report leading results on more than 30 benchmarks. It was the top paper on Hugging Face Daily Papers on October 23 with 239 upvotes.
items.why: One vision-language model for detection, OCR and segmentation can replace several CV services.

ecosystem.headline: Epic Games' official Unreal Engine plugin for Claude Code lets agents drive the Unreal Editor over MCP.

items.title: Epic ships official Unreal Engine plugin for Claude Code
items.body: Epic Games' plugin lets Claude Code control a running Unreal Editor through MCP, with hundreds of tools in 30+ toolsets for actors, Blueprints, materials, Niagara, Sequencer and automation tests. It includes an unreal-mcp skill and a SessionStart hook that marks the repo as an Unreal project. The repo has about 1.6k stars. Install: /plugin install unreal-engine-skills-for-claude-code@claude-plugins-official
items.why: It is a first-party example of a plugin that bundles an MCP server, a skill and a SessionStart hook.

items.title: kubernetes-mcp-server v0.0.69 adds a Go-native K8s agent bridge
items.body: kubernetes-mcp-server is an Apache-2.0 MCP server that lets AI agents work with Kubernetes and OpenShift, including Helm. It is written in Go and talks to the API server directly. Version 0.0.69 is out and the repo has about 2,180 stars.
items.why: DevOps teams get a single-binary MCP server for Kubernetes, OpenShift and Helm without kubectl wrappers.

items.title: Meridian browser gives Claude Code tab control via MCP
items.body: Meridian is a new open-source, Arc-style browser for AI agents. Its MCP server lets Claude Code read and click tabs. Access levels are off, read only, ask first and full control.
items.why: Browser automation with tiered permissions fits safe agent setups.

x-desk.headline: OpenAI's post on training frontier models without live internet led AI on X with 12.8k likes.
x-desk.note: Read 28 posts in 3 searches; 4 from searches 1 and 2 passed the filter.

items.title: NVIDIA ships RTX Remix for Minecraft: Java Edition
items.body: NVIDIA released RTX Remix for Minecraft: Java Edition. Creators can remaster the game with path-traced lighting and use DLSS for performance. It is available through NVIDIA GeForce and RTX Spark channels.
items.why: It shows path tracing and AI upscaling reaching mainstream modding tools on RTX hardware.

gadgets.headline: Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, went on sale in 70 countries and regions on October 23.
gadgets.note: Only three official launches in the last 48 hours were confirmed from the sources that loaded.

items.title: iPhone Duo goes on sale in 70 countries and regions
items.body: Apple's iPhone Duo is on sale in 70 countries and regions after one week of pre-orders. It has 12GB RAM and 256GB or 512GB storage. UK prices are £1,999 and £2,199, and German prices are €2,299 and €2,549. New online orders now show January delivery, and store stock is limited.
items.why: Apple's first foldable is now in buyers' hands, and new online orders already slip to January.

items.title: Oppo Find X10 and X10 Pro Max launch in India
items.body: The Find X10 Pro Max uses the Dimensity 9600 Pro, three 200MP rear cameras and a 6.78-inch display. The Find X10 uses the Dimensity 9600M and a 6.59-inch display. Both have an 8,000mAh battery, 80W wired and 50W wireless charging, and IP66/IP68/IP69 ratings. India prices start at Rs 1,39,999 for the Find X10 and Rs 1,99,999 for the Pro Max, and sales start on October 29.
items.why: Two flagship camera phones with 8,000mAh batteries reach India, with sales from October 29.

items.title: OnePlus confirms Ace 7 and Ace 7 Pro launch on October 29
items.body: OnePlus will launch the Ace 7 and Ace 7 Pro in China on October 29. The Ace 7 uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5V, and the Ace 7 Pro uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. OnePlus showed each model in black, white and a third colour.
items.why: New Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 phones from OnePlus often lead to global and India models later.

tech-pulse.headline: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro, an open-weight model that scores close to Claude Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0.
tech-pulse.note: The Hacker News page for yesterday (front?day) did not load, so this run used the live front page.

items.title: Calif demonstrates iPhone exploits at Hexacon, including one-click Signal attack
items.body: Security firm Calif showed a series of iPhone hacking demos at the Hexacon conference in Paris. The demos include a one-click attack on the Signal app and a teaser about iMessage. The post does not explain the exploits or name an iOS version. It says the details will be released later.
items.why: New iPhone attack chains affect mobile security plans and patch tracking for every iOS fleet.

items.title: Block previews Dessa, a speech-only full-duplex conversation model
items.body: Dessa is a research-preview speech-to-speech model from Block that can listen and talk at the same time. It was trained from scratch on human speech only, with no text and no pretrained models, on one NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 system. Block says it runs locally on a MacBook Pro M4 Max or better. Early access goes to a small group of AI safety researchers.
items.why: A voice model that listens and talks at the same time and runs on a laptop points to new local voice agents.

items.title: Astral connects uv and ty with new uv check command
items.body: Astral released an experimental integration between uv and ty. ty can now type-check PEP 723 scripts in the CLI and editor, and a new uv check command runs ty on a project. The features need uv 0.12.3 or later and ty 0.0.76 or later. In VS Code, set ty.experimental.useUv to on.
items.why: Python teams get type checking for scripts and projects from the same tool they use for packages.

aws-news.headline: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock now supports domain filtering and user location controls.

items.title: Bedrock Web Search adds domain filtering and user location
items.body: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock now supports domain filtering and optional user location controls on the web_search tool in an OpenAI Responses API request. A filter can list up to 100 allowed domains or up to 100 blocked domains. The features are available in US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon) and AWS GovCloud (US-West).
items.why: Agent builders can limit which sites grounded answers come from and tailor results by region.

items.title: EMR on EKS cuts the EMR charge by 30 percent
items.body: Amazon EMR reduced the EMR charge for EMR on EKS by 30 percent for both per-vCPU-hour and per-GB-hour charges. Amazon EKS charges do not change. The new price applies automatically in all Regions where EMR on EKS is offered.
items.why: Spark teams on Kubernetes pay less with no change to their setup.

items.title: Transit Gateway and Cloud WAN add managed 1:1 NAT
items.body: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now provide managed one-to-one NAT on attachments through Regional Private NAT Gateway. This lets networks with overlapping CIDRs, such as two companies that both use 10.0.0.0/16, connect without custom return-traffic rules. It is available in all commercial Regions where these services run.
items.why: Networks with overlapping IP ranges can connect without renumbering or NAT appliances.

items.title: Amazon Corretto October 2026 quarterly security updates
items.body: Amazon released quarterly updates for Corretto LTS builds of OpenJDK: 27.0.1.0.10, 25.0.5.0.9, 21.0.13.0.10, 17.0.21.0.10, 11.0.33.0.9 and 8u512. AWS describes them as security and critical updates. Linux users can get them through Apt, Yum or Apk repositories.
items.why: Java fleets on Corretto should roll out these security and critical fixes.

items.title: Amazon Connect Global Resiliency adds persistent chat across Regions
items.body: Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now supports persistent chat across linked AWS Regions. End users can resume earlier chats with full context, metadata and transcripts, so agents see the whole history. Customers turn it on by onboarding to Global routing.
items.why: Contact centres keep full chat history when traffic fails over to a linked Region.

briefing:
Good morning. This is The Nexos Daily for Sunday, the twenty-fifth of October.

The lead story: OpenAI removed live internet access from all frontier model training. Its models now browse and search a large cached copy of the web instead. OpenAI made the change after an internal model reached the internet through a DNS misconfiguration in September.

Security next. OpenAI's red-team agents found an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in the Brotli compression library. Node.js, Python HTTP clients and Envoy include Brotli, and patched versions are out. Update now if your services decode compressed traffic. Also on Hacker News: researchers showed iPhone exploits at Hexacon, including a one-click attack through Signal.

In the Claude world, Anthropic gave the Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation at the Linux Foundation. More than seventy platforms already use the format. Claude Code version two point one point three ten makes the Monitor tool and plugin monitors work on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, and the release before it hardens the sandbox and MCP permissions. Anthropic now runs the Claude API directly for Google Cloud customers, with Opus five point five fast mode. And Epic Games shipped an official Unreal Engine plugin for Claude Code.

Models: Moonshot released Kimi K three point one Pro, a mixture-of-experts model with one million tokens of context, at two dollars per million input tokens. Its open-weight release removes cyberattack training data.

Chips and research: NVIDIA launched Minerva, which joins GPU, network and storage telemetry into one live map of an AI data center to predict failures. A new open model, IQuest Q one, targets agentic command-line work with three hundred twenty billion parameters. And a paper on Deep Fusion Memory adds knowledge to a model without online retrieval.

For AWS engineers: Bedrock web search adds domain filters and user location. EMR on EKS is thirty percent cheaper. And Transit Gateway and Cloud WAN add managed one-to-one NAT.

In gadgets, Apple's iPhone Duo foldable is on sale in seventy countries and regions.

On the trending page, the fastest-growing new repo is an MCP replay tool, which gained one hundred sixty-seven stars on its first day.

It is Sunday, so the Week in review is out too, with the top ten stories of the week and the skill of the week.

That is the briefing. Every story links to its source in the paper. Have a good day.
